title: Why You Can't Buy a Chinese EV in America #shorts

scenes.text: A brand-new electric car for about ten thousand dollars exists. But in America, you basically can't buy one.
In China, the new BYD Seagull starts under ten thousand dollars. The average new electric car here costs about fifty-six thousand.
Wall number one: tariffs. Chinese-made electric cars face more than one hundred percent in import taxes.
Wall number two: software. From model year 2027, cars with Chinese connected-car software are banned from sale. Washington warns of data leaks, and even remote control.
Meanwhile, Canada cut its tariff to about six percent for up to forty-nine thousand cars a year.
Supporters say the walls protect jobs and data. Critics say Americans pay more. Should they be allowed in? Follow EV Drive.
